title: Ingesting RelayShield Threat Intelligence into Elastic Security
excerpt: RelayShield exposes its IOC corpus over both TAXII 2.1 and the MISP API. Elastic Security ships native Threat Intel integrations for both, so no custom code, connector, or middleware...
html:
RelayShield exposes its IOC corpus over both TAXII 2.1 and the MISP API. Elastic Security

ships native Threat Intel integrations for both, so no custom code, connector, or middleware is

required — this is a configuration task, not a development one.

What you get: 4.5M+ indicators sourced from 83+ criminal Telegram marketplaces and 20 authoritative

feeds, flowing into Elastic's logs-ti_* indices where they automatically enrich alerts and power

Indicator Match detection rules.

Requirements: a RelayShield API key with a Threat Intelligence subscription, and Elastic Stack

8.x or later (Elastic Cloud or self-managed).

Option A — TAXII 2.1 (recommended)

Elastic's Threat Intel TAXII 2.x integration polls a TAXII server on a schedule and normalises

STIX objects into ECS.

1. Confirm your key works

curl -s https://api.relayshield.net/v1/intel/taxii/ \
  -H "X-RS-API-KEY: YOUR_API_KEY"

A valid key returns the TAXII discovery document:

{
  "title": "RelayShield Threat Intelligence",
  "description": "RelayShield TAXII 2.1 server — 4,500,000+ IOCs ...",
  "api_roots": ["https://api.relayshield.net/v1/intel/taxii/"]
}

Without a valid key you get 401 with {"title": "Unauthorized", ...}. That is the correct

response, and a useful way to confirm the endpoint is reachable before adding credentials.

2. List available collections

curl -s https://api.relayshield.net/v1/intel/taxii/collections/ \
  -H "X-RS-API-KEY: YOUR_API_KEY"

The collection ID you want is iocs.

Older documentation referred to this collection as relayshield-iocs. Both identifiers are
accepted, so an existing configuration using the longer form keeps working.

3. Add the integration in Kibana

Management → Integrations → Threat Intel TAXII 2.x → Add

FieldValue
Server URLhttps://api.relayshield.net/v1/intel/taxii/
Collection IDiocs
Authentication typeHTTP header
Header nameX-RS-API-KEY
Header valueyour RelayShield API key
Interval1h (start here; tighten only if your use case needs it)

Leave the default Initial interval unless you specifically want a large historical backfill on

first run.

4. Confirm data is arriving

In Discover, query the threat intel data stream:

data_stream.dataset : "ti_taxii.indicator"

Indicators land with threat.indicator.type set to domain-name, ipv4-addr, url, email-addr

or file depending on the IOC.

Option B — MISP

If you already run Elastic's Threat Intel MISP integration, RelayShield can be added as an

additional source rather than replacing your existing one.

curl -s https://api.relayshield.net/v1/intel/misp/ \
  -H "X-RS-API-KEY: YOUR_API_KEY"

Management → Integrations → Threat Intel MISP → Add

FieldValue
URLhttps://api.relayshield.net/v1/intel/misp/
AuthenticationX-RS-API-KEY: YOUR_API_KEY
Interval1h

Event detail is available at /v1/intel/misp/event/.

Using the data

Enrichment

Once indicators are flowing, Elastic's built-in Threat Intel enrichment automatically matches

them against your existing logs. No rule authoring needed — matches appear on the alert under

threat.enrichments.

Indicator Match rule

For explicit detection, create a rule under Security → Rules → Create new rule → Indicator Match:

SettingValue
Index patternsyour source logs (e.g. logs-, filebeat-)
Indicator indexlogs-ti_*
Indicator mappingdestination.ip → threat.indicator.ip
dns.question.name → threat.indicator.url.domain
url.full → threat.indicator.url.full

Set severity to match your triage process. Because RelayShield's corpus is sourced from criminal

marketplaces rather than general reputation feeds, a match generally warrants investigation rather

than informational logging.

A note on timing

RelayShield's Telegram-sourced indicators typically surface 24–72 hours ahead of public feeds,

because the pipeline collects from the marketplaces where credentials and infrastructure are sold

rather than waiting for downstream aggregation. That lead time is the reason to run this alongside,

not instead of, your existing feeds.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCause
401 UnauthorizedKey is missing, wrong, or lacks a TI subscription. The TI endpoints require an active TI plan, separate from PAYG API access.
404 on /v1/taxii/...Wrong path — the prefix is /v1/intel/taxii/, not /v1/taxii/.
Integration added, no documentsCheck the interval has elapsed, then confirm the collection ID is iocs (or relayshield-iocs — both are accepted).
Indicators arrive but never matchVerify your indicator mapping field names against the ECS fields actually present in your source logs.

Support

support@relayshield.net — include the integration type (TAXII or MISP) and the Kibana error text

if there is one.
